readmeHtml:
Stop Slop

A skill for removing AI tells from prose.

What this is

AI writing has patterns. Predictable phrases, structures, rhythms. This skill teaches Claude (or any LLM) to catch and remove them.

Skill Structure

stop-slop/
├── SKILL.md              # Core instructions
├── references/
│   ├── phrases.md        # Phrases to remove
│   ├── structures.md     # Structural patterns to avoid
│   └── examples.md       # Before/after transformations
├── README.md
└── LICENSE

Quick start

Claude Code: Add this folder as a skill.

Claude Projects: Upload SKILL.md and reference files to project knowledge.

Custom instructions: Copy core rules from SKILL.md.

API calls: Include SKILL.md in your system prompt. Reference files load on demand.

What it catches

Banned phrases - Throat-clearing openers, emphasis crutches, business jargon, all adverbs, vague declaratives, meta-commentary. See references/phrases.md.

Structural clichés - Binary contrasts, negative listings, dramatic fragmentation, rhetorical setups, false agency, narrator-from-a-distance voice, passive voice. See references/structures.md.

Sentence-level rules - No Wh- sentence starters, no em dashes, no staccato fragmentation, no lazy extremes, active voice required.

Scoring

Rate 1-10 on each dimension:

Dimension Question
Directness Statements or announcements?
Rhythm Varied or metronomic?
Trust Respects reader intelligence?
Authenticity Sounds human?
Density Anything cuttable?

Below 35/50: revise.

Author

Hardik Pandya

License

MIT. Use freely, share widely.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A browser extension, API, and agent skill to detect and filter out low-quality, AI-generated content from prose.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Stop-Slop is a comprehensive tool designed to combat the proliferation of predictable, low-effort AI-generated content. It functions as a browser extension, an API, and a distinct skill that can be loaded into agents like Claude. The system analyzes text to identify the metronomic rhythms, generic transitions, and structural markers typical of unedited LLM output. Whether hiding boilerplate SEO spam in a browser or instructing an LLM to revise its own prose for authenticity and directness, Stop-Slop drastically improves the signal-to-noise ratio of written content. This tool explicitly targets and removes common AI tells from generated prose to ensure it maintains a natural, human-like voice.
keyFeatures: Heuristic Pattern Matching: Identifies common phrases, repetitive structural markers, and generic openers typical of unedited AI outputs.
Agent Skill Integration: Provides a SKILL.md file and reference lists that teach LLMs to catch and remove their own writing 'tells'.
Real-Time Page Filtering: The browser extension analyzes and modifies the DOM on the fly to hide or flag detected boilerplate content.
Adjustable Sensitivity Thresholds: Allows users to tune how aggressively the tool filters content based on a multi-point scoring system.
API Access: Provides a programmatic endpoint for developers to check text strings against the detection model.
Pattern Recognition: Identifies highly repetitive synthetic phrasing structures to replace them with natural language.

useCases.title: Prose Self-Correction
useCases.description: Writers upload the skill folder into their Claude Project to ensure the AI generates authentic, direct prose without typical throat-clearing.

useCases.title: Improving Search Results
useCases.description: Users install the extension to automatically collapse generic, AI-generated introductions when searching for technical answers.

useCases.title: Content Moderation
useCases.description: Forum administrators use the API to automatically flag incoming posts that exhibit a high density of known AI structural markers.

useCases.title: Quality Assurance
useCases.description: Editors use the tool's 50-point scoring system to evaluate submissions and ensure writers aren't relying heavily on raw LLM outputs.

useCases.title: Editorial Review
useCases.description: Editors automatically clean drafted articles to ensure published content sounds entirely human-written.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: General internet users wanting a cleaner browsing experience, developers needing moderation APIs, and writers aiming to improve AI-assisted prose.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Install the extension from the Chrome Web Store or load the SKILL.md into Claude Code.
